summary: USB bring-up ladder L0-L8 of the NAT-040 plan as C: a generator (derive.py) compiles the vendor function bodies at the pinned SHA 417484173abc2c4fa93e738ea82ad9f2e84911b1 into a 111-op table (src/ladder_regs.h, ladder_ops.json), cross-checked kind/mask/value-wise against the NAT-040 plan, and a small interpreter (src/ladder.c) runs it over the NAT-041 port contract; L0-L2 are read-only and the default image (no LAD_WRITING_RUNGS) has no store and no delay compiled in; L6-L8 (src/ladder_usb.c) hand over to the unmodified NAT-041 usbmon engine. test_nat045.py: Ran 77 tests, OK (Table, Generator, Ladder, DefaultBuild, Usb, Aarch64 layers; unicorn+capstone+zig present, nothing skipped); mutation check 498 killed + 5 documented-equivalent of 503, 0 survived, 0 invalid. Nothing was run on the phone.
evidence_category: host-test (generator, x86 register-level model, unicorn instruction-level run of the compiled aarch64 ladder); not a measurement of the S24

acceptance.1_ladder_as_c: src/ladder.c + generated src/ladder_regs.h: one rung function per ladder rung with the distinct error codes LAD_ERR(rung, READBACK|TIMEOUT|STATE|NOTALIVE|CFG|DISABLED) and a per-op record/stage log; every address, mask, value and the delays come from derive.py re-reading the pinned vendor sources (derive.py --check exits 0; any constant that differs from the pinned text, or any vendor statement the generator cannot model, is a DeriveError, exit 2); the 22 SET rows are additionally recomputed with the C compiler's own bit-field layout of the vendor headers; the plan cross-check is kind-, mask- and value-aware; L0-L2 read-only, default build stops after L2 and has no store/delay (DefaultBuild layer, and the unicorn run of the default object shows no device store).
acceptance.2_model_and_unknowns: test_support/plat.c (register file with strict access rules, gating, follow/stuck/flip fault injection) and devmodel.py + a64sim.py run the compiled x86 and aarch64 objects; tests show the writing rungs happen only when enabled, in the cited order, with the stated virtual-time delays (500/500/10/10/10/1000/28/2500 us) and that a failed read-back stops the ladder at its row without a retry; the unknowns U1-U8 of NAT-040 are carried as named probe results in the lad_state record (README.md, section 'The unknowns of NAT-040 as probe results'), none guessed; mutation check: 503 mutants (136 C, 61 generator, 306 table fields) - 498 killed, 5 equivalent (each justified in mutate_nat045.py), 0 survived, 0 invalid, 0 anchor errors.
acceptance.3_engine_link: src/ladder_usb.c links the unmodified NAT-041 engine (usbmon.c hash below equals the file NAT-041 recorded) after the last rung in the host build (Usb layer: lad_usb_start -> usbmon_init, lad_usb_wait polling the engine for CONNECTDONE and the host nonce against the NAT-041 DWC3 model); nothing ran on the phone.

established: The generated table equals what the pinned vendor sources and the NAT-040 plan give (derive.py --check exit 0); 111 ops, rung starts 0,0,2,5,26,27,111.

The compiled ladder (x86 and aarch64 objects) performs the table's accesses in order against the strict register-file model, stops at the first failed read-back with the documented code and op, never writes in the default build, and never writes a block the PMU state says is off.

Every mutant of the ladder C, the generator and every field of every table row either makes the suite fail or is a documented equivalent; run 004 is the run of the recorded tree (runs 002 and 003 are superseded, see README).
NAT-041 engine files linked unmodified: usbmon.c 37a53cbaa8887958, usbmon.h 37fafc1fc9b23f0f.
not_established: Anything about the real S24: that these registers behave as the vendor driver sequence assumes, that the PMU power-on of pd_hsi0 works from the loader, that the eUSB2 PHY comes up without the repeater/regulator/SMC prerequisites (U1-U8 stay unknowns; each is a named probe result for NAT-043 to read), or that the DWC3 at 0x17900000 answers.

That the register-file model is faithful: it encodes one reading of the vendor driver and of NAT-040; where the generator and the model share a misreading the tests cannot notice. The mutation check shows the tests detect single changes to the code, not that the specification is right.
The SMC step (DTZPC 0x17810204, plan 0.02) is not attempted by the ladder; a platform that needs it fails at the NOTALIVE/READBACK rung and says so.
Caches, MMU attributes, SError and real bus timing (unicorn has none of them; the virtual time of the x86 model is exact by construction).
findings: The plan cross-check was too lenient (a PMUCAL_WRITE row was satisfied by the ladder's read of the same register, a PMUCAL_READ row by the wait): fixed in derive.py (kind/mask/value-aware), generated header unchanged, ladder_ops.json plan annotations moved.

Tests of the L7/L8 polling were vacuous because the NAT-041 model polls the engine itself after each host step; SET masks and LOAD addresses were invisible from a zero register file; both fixed with behavioural tests (non-polling model, exact counts, C-compiler oracle, same-register invariant).

Run 003 left one survivor (plan READ row satisfied by a WAIT of equal mask and value); a test was added and run 004 recorded. A first attempt at run 004 crashed with 'Disk quota exceeded' on the shared /tmp tmpfs (unrelated projects fill it) and was repeated with TMPDIR on the project disk; no result of the crashed attempt is used.
